question.text: Fund GMS holds long positions in Indian large-cap equities, long positions in WTI crude oil futures, and short positions in USD/INR and GBP/INR futures. This position mix is MOST consistent with which Category III AIF strategy?

answer.text: Global Macro Strategy with a Long-Short overlay

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.2.2 (Global-Macro Strategy) and Example 11.5, a fund taking long and short positions across multiple asset classes (equities, currencies, commodities) based on macro-economic views is pursuing Global Macro. With net long equity/commodity and net short currency, it also qualifies as a Long-Short overlay within the macro framework. The Trap: Convertible Arb needs a convertible bond and its underlying stock — not a multi-asset mix. Merger Arb needs a specific deal. Pre-IPO is single-stock unlisted equity. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests Global Macro at a strategy level; XIX-C tests the classification call — how to name the strategy correctly in the PPM risk-factors section.
